Patience of hope: he praises these
- Verse 4, election: we'll deal with this mainly in Ephesians, but in three weeks Paul had taught them everything, Christ's resurrection, mission, the Second Coming. It's not that we chose God; God chose us. At first glance it looks like I decided to believe in Jesus, but even that is within God's predestination.
2장입니다. 바울은 데살로니가에서 자신이 했던 사역들이 어땠었는지 쭉 설: Chapter 2. Paul explains at length what his ministry in Thessalonica was like. Verse 2: he says he suffered a lot in Philippi but still preached the gospel to you, right? Paul nearly died there, remember. And he says that to please God we didn't use deceit or dishonest methods, didn't flatter, and weren't greedy. And though he could have acted with authority as an apostle, he says, I was gentle, like nursing a baby. Why? Because the Thessalonian believers were still young... he preached for three weeks and left, after all.
9절 보세요. 바울이 폐를 끼치지 않으려고 일하면서 복음을 전했다고 하죠: Look at verse 9. Paul says he worked while preaching the gospel so as not to be a burden, right? What was Paul's work? Making tents. That's why today people who do mission work with their own money are sometimes called tentmaker missionaries.
그러면서 10절 우리는 너희 앞에서 거룩하고 옳고 흠 없이 행했다. 왜?: And verse 10: we behaved holily, justly and unblameably before you. Why? The second half of verse 12: so that you would walk worthy of God. Folks, if the person preaching the gospel isn't holy, isn't just, and has lots of faults... the people receiving it won't walk worthy before God.
13절 보시면요, 다행이도 데살로니가 사람들이 바울이 전하는 말을 사람의: Look at verse 13: thankfully, the Thessalonians didn't hear what Paul preached as the word of men, but received it as the word of God. So in verse 14 he says the Thessalonians followed the example of the churches in Judea and reached the point of enduring suffering. Look at verses 15-16, it says the Jews persecuted the church, right? They followed the example of the suffering of the saints there and endured persecution from their own countrymen. So he's thankful. Folks, raising people into believers like this in three weeks, is that easy? Or hard?
이어서 바울은 몇 번 보고싶어서 가려고 했는데 사탄이 못가게 막았다고 하: Then Paul says he tried to go several times because he wanted to see them, but Satan hindered him, and he says, if I receive a crown when I meet Jesus, that crown is you. Paul's time with the Thessalonian believers may have been only about three weeks, but his love for them was second to none.
3장입니다. 그래서 누구를 보낸데요? 2절. 디모데를 보낸다. 너희를 굳: Chapter 3. So who does he send? Verse 2. He sends Timothy. To establish you and keep you from being shaken in afflictions. Why? Verse 4. I told you we would suffer affliction, and it turned out just as I said.
6절 그래서 디모데가 돌아와서 하는 말이 데살로니가 교인들의 믿음이 대폭: Verse 6: so Timothy comes back and reports that the Thessalonian believers' faith has grown a lot and they miss Paul's team like crazy. He says hearing that, he was greatly comforted.
그래서 무슨 선물을 줄까 하다가 직접 얼굴을 보러 가겠다. 가서 부족한: So, thinking about what gift to give them, he says, I'll come see you in person. I'll come and supply what's lacking in your faith. So I've made up my mind too. Even if I have to keep going till dawn today, I will supply what's lacking in you all.
4장입니다. 그러므로 끝으로 하나만 말할께 하면서 6장까지 가요. 바울도: Chapter 4. "Finally, one last thing," he says, and goes on through chapter 6. Paul's a bit like me, isn't he? Geniuses think alike. So what does he urge? Keep doing what you're doing, even more. In other words, you're doing well, right? And then what does he say? Verse 3: this is the will of God. Holiness. We said holiness means being set apart, right? Abstain from fornication, treat your wife with honor, don't follow lust, don't wrong your brother.
9절 형제 사랑은 너희가 잘 하고 있다. 10절 더욱 힘써라. 11절 조: Verse 9: as for brotherly love, you're doing well. Verse 10: do it even more. Verse 11: quietly do your own work well. So that you won't be in need.
13절 형제들아 자는 자들에 관하여는 너희가 알지 못하기를 원치 이니하노: Verse 13: "But I would not have you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning them which are asleep"... A double negative is a strong positive, right? I really want you to know about those who have died. So that you don't grieve like people who have no hope..
뭐냐면... 15-17절 눈으로 죽 훑어 보세요. 예수 안에서 죽은 사람: What is it... skim through verses 15-17 with your eyes. What happens to people who died in Jesus? They're resurrected. Especially look at verse 16, an important source for later when we study Revelation: Jesus will descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trumpet. So everyone today calling himself Jesus is a fake. The real Jesus has to come down from heaven. Anyone else is either a con man or an antichrist.
그 때 그리스도 안에서 죽은 자들이 먼저 살아나고 그 때까지 살아남은 사: At that time the dead in Christ rise first, and those still alive by then are caught up in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air. Comfort one another with these words.
4. 특별히 주목해야 될 부분\n 1) 예수님의 재림은 우리에게는 도적같:
4. Parts to pay special attention to
 1) Jesus' Second Coming will not come upon us like a thief.
<살전5:1~6> 형제들아 때와 시기에 관하여는 너희에게 쓸 것이 없음은:
<1 Thess 5:1~6> But of the times and the seasons, brethren, ye have no need that I write unto you. For yourselves know perfectly that the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night. For when they shall say, Peace and safety; then sudden destruction cometh upon them, as travail upon a woman with child; and they shall not escape. But ye, brethren, are not in darkness, that that day should overtake you as a thief. Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness. Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober.
 - Jesus' Second Coming on the last day comes like a thief upon them, the people of the world, but it does not come upon us like a thief. If you study the Bible well, especially Revelation, you won't know the day, the date, the month, the hour and so on, but you'll be able to discern the time. I'll explain it later when we get to Revelation, and you'll all come to know it.
 2) The will of God
<살전5:12~18> 형제들아 우리가 너희에게 구하노니 너희 가운데서 수:
<1 Thess 5:12~18> And we beseech you, brethren, to know them which labour among you, and are over you in the Lord, and admonish you; and to esteem them very highly in love for their work's sake. And be at peace among yourselves. Now we exhort you, brethren, warn them that are unruly, comfort the feebleminded, support the weak, be patient toward all men. See that none render evil for evil unto any man; but ever follow that which is good, both among yourselves, and to all men. Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks: for this is the will of God in Christ Jesus concerning you.
 - People usually say only verses 16~18 are the will of God, but you have to circle from verse 12. What does it say right before "Rejoice evermore"? It says always follow what is good, right? You should rejoice always while following what is good; you shouldn't rejoice always while following evil, right? So limiting the will of God to just "Rejoice evermore, pray without ceasing, in every thing give thanks" is wrong. It's only because it has a nice rhythm and is handy to pluck out and use; in fact the will of God isn't just that, that's my point.
<살전5:19~22> 성령을 소멸치 말며 예언을 멸시치 말고 범사에 헤아:
<1 Thess 5:19~22> Quench not the Spirit. Despise not prophesyings. Prove all things; hold fast that which is good. Abstain from all appearance of evil.
 - And from verse 19 on, isn't that the will of God too? It is the will of God. So that's why we look at the whole Bible, so we don't make this kind of mistake.
26절에 보면 ‘입맞춤으로 모든 형제에게 문안하라’는 말이 나오죠? 베드:
In verse 26 it says ‘Greet all the brethren with an holy kiss,’ right? 1 Peter 5:14, Romans 16:16 and 1 Corinthians 16:20 say the same thing. Paul says this to almost every church he sends a letter to. Greeting with a kiss was how people of fairly high status greeted each other at the time. It wasn't done to slaves or servants. When Paul says greet all the brethren, he means: servant, free man, slave, no matter who, give everyone that same greeting you normally give each other.
 3) Paul's letter that caused a problem in the Thessalonian church

For the Lord himself shall descend from heaven with a shout, with the voice of the archangel, and with the trump of God: and the dead in Christ shall rise first:
<살전5:23> 평강의 하나님이 친히 너희로 온전히 거룩하게 하시고 또:

 - Because he talked about the Lord's coming at the end of every chapter like this, the Thessalonians said Jesus was coming any moment, and didn't go to school, didn't go to work, and just went around making trouble.
이 이야기를 들은 바울이 깜짝 놀라서 다시 편지를 쓰는데 예수님이 오시긴: Hearing this, Paul was shocked and wrote again, saying Jesus is coming, but not that soon, and the follow-up letter he wrote is 2 Thessalonians.
